questions.q: What does `ORDER BY invoice_amount DESC` do?
options: Filters out invoices under a certain amount
Groups invoices by amount
Sorts the result set by invoice_amount, largest first
Deletes the smallest invoices from the table
questions.explain: ORDER BY sorts the final result set. DESC means descending (largest first); the default without DESC is ascending.

questions.q: When does `FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY` take effect relative to `ORDER BY` in the same query?
options: Before ORDER BY runs
At the exact same time, with no defined order
FETCH FIRST cannot be combined with ORDER BY
After ORDER BY has already sorted the result
questions.explain: FETCH FIRST applies after the sort, which is why it reliably returns the correct top N rows.

questions.q: Why does the legacy ROWNUM pattern require wrapping the sorted query in an outer query, as in `SELECT ... FROM (SELECT ... ORDER BY ...) WHERE ROWNUM <= 10`?
options: Because ROWNUM is assigned to rows before ORDER BY takes effect in that same query block, so sorting must happen first in an inner query
Because ROWNUM only works inside subqueries, never in a top-level query
Because Oracle requires every query to have at least two SELECT statements
There is no real reason — it's just a stylistic convention
questions.explain: ROWNUM numbers rows as they're produced, before ORDER BY in the same block reorders them — so the sort has to happen in an inner query first.

questions.q: Which clause, introduced in Oracle Database 12c, is the modern ANSI-standard way to cap a result set after sorting?
options: TOP
FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY
LIMIT
ROWNUM
questions.explain: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY is Oracle's 12c+ ANSI-standard row-limiting clause, used throughout this course going forward.

questions.q: What does `OFFSET 10 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY` return?
options: The first 10 rows only
Every row except the first 10
An error — OFFSET cannot be combined with FETCH NEXT
Rows 11 through 20 of the sorted result
questions.explain: OFFSET skips the first 10 rows, then FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY returns the next 10 — rows 11-20, useful for paging.
